_comment: DYNAMIC DETAIL ROUTES — the pages certify.mjs's static sweep can never see. routes.json holds the 54 NAV destinations; a record page only exists once a record does, so its URL cannot be written down in advance. The sweep therefore reported ZERO raw-id findings across 270 visits while SalesOrderDetail was printing a Firestore document id as visible content. Each entry says how to REACH one representative record through the app's own governed list — never a hardcoded document id, which would rot the first time the sandbox is reseeded. A record that cannot be resolved is a FIXTURE_PRECONDITION failure, never a silent skip: a detail page nobody could open is exactly the state that hid the defect.

entities.label: Opportunity detail
entities._comment: WAS navigates:false with rowSelector 'tbody tr', and that was correct until 2026-08-26: an Opportunity had no record route, so selecting a row filled the aside and the URL never changed. The consequence was that the Quick Gate reported this entity RESOLVED while never opening a record page — the exact blind spot the header of this file was written about, reopened one entity over. The per-record route exists now (/customers/opportunities/:opportunityId over the governed getOpportunityContext, deployed bc2d7ccd), so this entity certifies the record page itself. SELECTOR CHANGED 2026-08-27 (North Star P1v4, DECISIONS #135). It was '.fo-sales-detail__open-record a' — the WORKSPACE PANE's own 'Open OPP-…' link, chosen because the workspace AUTO-SELECTED the first row on load, so the pane was populated before any click. P1v4 retired that pane and its auto-selection deliberately, which took the selector with it: the gate then reported 'no rows at /customers/opportunities?view=all' against a list that renders 14. A harness assumption wearing a fixture failure's clothes — the exact confusion this file's header warns about, one product generation later. It is now the collection's own row anchor: a real <a> to the record route, and the thing a user actually clicks, so the harness no longer depends on any auto-selection behaviour continuing to exist. ?view=all is still required because the sandbox has few OPEN opportunities — the very condition that made this detail unreachable before the history views landed. expectRoutePattern forbids a second path segment on purpose, so landing on /customers/opportunities/sales-order/<id> is a resolution FAILURE rather than a quiet pass.

entities.label: Contact (on the Account record)
entities._comment: Contacts have no route of their own — /customers/contacts is retired and redirects. A Contact is reached as a section of the Account record, so this probes the same destination as `account` and exists to state that explicitly rather than let a reader assume Contact detail went unswept.

entities.label: Part detail
entities._comment: The Parts list opens a Part from a LINK inside the row, not from a row click -- the row itself has no handler. Resolving by row click reported a truthful FIXTURE_PRECONDITION failure (it genuinely did not navigate), which is the harness being right about the wrong question: the record IS reachable, just not that way.
